skill.name: configuring-better-auth
skill.description: Configure Better Auth for OAuth 2.1, OIDC, PKCE, and SSO workflows. Use this skill to plan an auth server, integrate Next.js clients, verify tokens with JWKS, and manage token refresh patterns.
skill.summary: Set up Better Auth OAuth, OIDC, PKCE, SSO clients, JWKS verification, and token workflows for Next.js applications.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown code fences, TypeScript template literals, localhost URLs, and legitimate Better Auth configuration examples. Confirmed issues are a third-party MCP setup recommendation, unsafe JWKS private key guidance, and several authentication design problems in the examples. No prompt-injection text was found in the reviewed skill files.

remediation.issue: The skill recommends connecting to a third-party Better Auth MCP server.
remediation.suggestion: Explain the trust boundary, require explicit user confirmation, and document what project context may be sent to the remote MCP service.

remediation.issue: The JWKS example disables private key encryption for simplicity.
remediation.suggestion: Remove disablePrivateKeyEncryption from production examples, or clearly restrict it to local development with documented key management controls.

remediation.issue: The auth server reference recommends localStorage for OAuth tokens.
remediation.suggestion: Replace localStorage token guidance with server-side token exchange and httpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookie storage.

remediation.issue: The SSO callback example does not verify OAuth state before token exchange.
remediation.suggestion: Compare the returned state with the stored state, reject mismatches, and clear state after use.

remediation.issue: The PKCE verifier and callback URL examples use JavaScript-set cookies without full security controls.
remediation.suggestion: Use server-set encrypted cookies where possible, add Secure and SameSite attributes, and validate callback URLs as same-origin paths.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Token Storage Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The auth server reference shows access and refresh tokens stored in localStorage and later states that OAuth clients should only use localStorage tokens. This exposes bearer tokens to cross-site scripting and conflicts with the safer httpOnly cookie guidance elsewhere in the skill.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file directly uses localStorage for access_token and refresh_token handling, and the pitfall section explicitly endorses localStorage-only token use. This is a well-known browser token exposure risk.

semantic_findings.title: OAuth State Is Generated But Not Verified
semantic_findings.description: The SSO client generates and stores an OAuth state value, but the callback route only reads the returned state and does not compare it with the stored value before token exchange. Missing state validation weakens OAuth CSRF protection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code demonstrates state creation and callback parsing, but no equality check or rejection path appears in the callback example. The security checklist later says state should be verified, confirming the missing step matters.

semantic_findings.title: PKCE Verifier Stored In JavaScript-Accessible Cookies
semantic_findings.description: The examples copy the PKCE verifier into document.cookie without Secure or SameSite attributes in one reference, and JavaScript cannot set HttpOnly cookies. A stolen verifier can help complete an intercepted authorization code exchange.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly set PKCE values through document.cookie. This is not secret exfiltration by the skill, but it is unsafe implementation guidance for an authentication flow.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Callback URL Can Enable Open Redirects
semantic_findings.description: The SSO client stores a caller-provided callback URL in a cookie and later redirects to it after token exchange. Without same-origin or path-only validation, this pattern can become an authentication open redirect.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example accepts callbackUrl from signIn options and feeds it to NextResponse.redirect. The exploitability depends on how applications source that option, so confidence is high enough to flag but not absolute.

content.user_title: Configure Better Auth OAuth and SSO
content.value_statement: OAuth and SSO setups fail when token flows, PKCE, and client registration are inconsistent. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured Better Auth guide for server and client implementation.
actual_capabilities: Guides Better Auth OIDC provider setup for a centralized auth server.
Shows OAuth client registration patterns for public and confidential clients.
Explains PKCE authorization, token exchange, refresh, and logout flows.
Provides Next.js SSO client route, context, proxy, and cookie patterns.
Covers JWKS token verification and Better Auth JWT plugin configuration.
Includes email verification and admin-only client registration guidance.
limitations: Examples require adaptation to each project schema, routes, and deployment model.
The skill does not provision databases, email providers, OAuth credentials, or secrets.
Some examples require production hardening before use in a live authentication system.
Better Auth package behavior should be checked against current upstream documentation.

use_cases.title: Plan a Central Auth Server
use_cases.description: Design a Better Auth OIDC provider for several first-party applications.

use_cases.title: Integrate a Next.js SSO Client
use_cases.description: Add PKCE login, callback routes, cookies, token refresh, and logout to a client app.

use_cases.title: Review an OAuth Flow
use_cases.description: Check token storage, redirect handling, JWKS verification, and client registration choices.

prompt_templates.title: Plan My Auth Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new Better Auth deployment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the configuring-better-auth skill to plan a Better Auth OAuth and OIDC setup for my app. Ask me for the number of client apps, database choice, and required login features before recommending steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build an SSO Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate implementation for a Next.js client.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the configuring-better-auth skill to create an implementation checklist for a Next.js SSO client with PKCE, httpOnly token cookies, JWKS verification, refresh, and logout.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Auth Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing OAuth implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the configuring-better-auth skill to review my Better Auth OAuth flow. Focus on PKCE verifier handling, state validation, token storage, redirect URI validation, and JWKS verification.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-App Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the configuring-better-auth skill to design a multi-app SSO rollout. Include auth server responsibilities, public client registration, admin controls, JWKS strategy, refresh token rules, and production hardening tasks.

output_examples.input: I need one Better Auth server for two Next.js apps.
output_examples.output: Recommended architecture: one OIDC provider, two public clients with PKCE, exact redirect URIs, shared JWKS verification, and separate app logout handling.

output_examples.input: My callback route fails after login with a PKCE error.
output_examples.output: Likely causes: the verifier is lost before token exchange, the redirect URI changed, or the sign-in page did not preserve PKCE parameters.

output_examples.input: I want to check production readiness before launch.
output: Require HTTPS and exact redirect URI matching.
Use httpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies for tokens.
Verify state and ID tokens before creating an app session.
Keep client secrets out of browser code.

best_practices: Use PKCE for browser and mobile clients, and avoid client secrets in public code.
Store tokens in httpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies when a server route handles token exchange.
Validate state, redirect URIs, issuer, audience, token expiry, and JWKS signatures before trusting a session.
anti_patterns: Do not store access tokens or refresh tokens in localStorage for production applications.
Do not accept arbitrary callback URLs after login without same-origin validation.
Do not disable private key protection or skip state verification for convenience.

faq.question: What does this skill help configure?
faq.answer: It helps configure Better Auth OAuth, OIDC, PKCE, SSO clients, JWKS verification, token refresh, and logout flows.

faq.question: Is this only for Next.js?
faq.answer: Most examples target Next.js, but the OAuth, OIDC, PKCE, and JWKS patterns can guide other web frameworks.

faq.question: Does the skill create credentials for me?
faq.answer: No. You must create and store database, email, OAuth, and deployment secrets in your own environment.

faq.question: Can it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. Authentication code should still receive project-specific review, testing, and threat modeling before production use.

faq.question: Why does it mention MCP?
faq.answer: The skill suggests a Better Auth MCP server for guided setup, but users should review remote MCP trust before connecting it.

faq.question: What should I verify before launch?
faq.answer: Verify HTTPS, exact redirect URIs, state checks, token cookies, JWKS validation, rate limiting, email verification, and admin-only client registration.
